primitives.meaning: a formally created issue with a type, a severity and a related entity
entryFilters: an actionable issue is created with type, severity, related entity, SLA and source
the issue is not a duplicate of an open issue on the same underlying problem
an owner is known or determinable; an orphan goes to ownership resolution first

primitives.does: Capture the issue type, severity, related entity, SLA and source. Duplicates against the same underlying problem are reconciled here rather than worked twice

branches.label: Known
branches.test: the issue type and entity identify who owns it

branches.label: Unknown
branches.test: no owner can be determined from the issue itself

primitives.on: an issue with no determinable owner
carries: the issue and everything known about it
the fact that its SLA is already running, so assignment is not the start of the clock

primitives.does: Assign the owner and record the assignment, appended - who held an issue and when is part of its resolution history

cancelOn.meaning: the operational fix for the issue is recorded complete

primitives.reads: the issue re-read: fix completed or still open, and the current escalation level

primitives.does: Escalate one level: notify, then involve the team or manager, then reassign into a priority queue. Nothing customer-facing is sent because of this - an internal delay is our problem, not new information for them

branches.label: Levels remain
branches.test: a further level of escalation exists

branches.label: Exhausted
branches.test: the ladder has been walked and the issue is still open

primitives.on: an issue outliving its escalation ladder
carries: the full history: owners, escalations, elapsed time

primitives.asks: Does closure require the person to confirm?

branches.label: Confirmation required
branches.test: the fix is only verifiable from their side, or policy requires their agreement

branches.label: Not required
branches.test: the fix is verifiable operationally and policy allows closure on it

primitives.asks: Is there a permitted route to ask them?

branches.label: A route exists
branches.test: a permitted, deliverable destination for this person is available for issue correspondence

branches.label: No route
branches.test: no permitted destination is available, or the reporter cannot be reached on any of them

competition.precedence: an open issue under human ownership outranks automated retention and satisfaction outreach on the same account

orderedRoles.eligibleWhen: the confirmation question should reach the person where they can answer in their own time and keep the record of what was fixed
the issue was raised in the product and the person is active there

primitives.purpose: Ask whether the specific issue they raised is now resolved, against the fix that was actually performed.
primitives.brief: Ask whether the specific issue they raised is now resolved, against the fix that was actually performed. Waiting for a confirmation nobody was asked for is not a confirmation state, it is a timeout dressed as one

mustNotClaim: a fix that was not performed

primitives.label: CANONICAL_RULE

cancelOn.meaning: the person confirms the issue is resolved
the person says the issue is not resolved

primitives.reads: the issue re-read: confirmed, disputed, or silent

branches.label: Still not right
branches.test: they say the problem persists - the internal task completed and their issue did not

primitives.does: Close the issue, preserving the full resolution history: what was wrong, who owned it, what was done, when, and that the person confirmed it

Close under the bounded closure rule, recording explicitly that the fix completed and the person never confirmed. Confirmed and unconfirmed closures are different facts and are never written the same way - and, where closure was unconfirmed because no permitted route to the reporter existed, that reason is recorded as itself rather than as silence

primitives.reEntry: the same problem recurring is a new issue, linked to this one rather than reopening it
any later contact about the same problem enters knowing this was never verified, which is why the distinction is recorded
